chapter.title: Estimation, Hypothesis Tests and Confidence Procedures

missing_pieces.duty: ED26-P15-CH-hypothesis-tests-and-confidence-C008 (partial): The full proof promised by proved=annex:p15.binomial.most.powerful is not supplied. The explicit two-sided failure (n=1, p0=1/2, alpha=1/2: no test is most powerful at both p=1/4 and p=3/4) needs the maximum level-1/2 power at p=1/4 and the unique test that attains it. Annex lines 270-272 give this only as 'the reversed calculation forces a=1,b=0 for its maximum power 3/4'. The bound (3/4)a+(1/4)b=(1/4)(a+b)+(1/2)a<=3/4 and its equality case a=1, b=0 are never written, so a 'similarly' step stands in place of an owed proof step.

ED26-P15-CH-hypothesis-tests-and-confidence-C013 (partial): The full proof promised by proved=annex:p15.neyman.interval.construction is not supplied. The reconstruction S(x)=[l(x),u(x)] intersected with R needs both finite endpoints to lie in S(x). The lower endpoint is argued (annex 439-444), but the upper endpoint is given only as 'The same argument puts a finite u in S(x)' (annex 445-446). The missing step is choosing a finite a with l<a<u and applying condition 3 to (a,u).

ED26-P15-CH-hypothesis-tests-and-confidence-C016 (partial): The full proof promised by proved=annex:p15.binomial.confidence.coverage is not supplied. The exact-inversion statement (reject p iff T_{n,p}(K)<d or F_{n,p}(K)<d, with root endpoints accepted) needs p>u_n(k) <=> F_{n,p}(k)<d for k<n. Annex 593-598 gives this only as 'Similarly'. The missing written step derives it from the strict decrease of F_{n,p}(k) in p (thm:p15-binomial-tail-roots) and F_{n,u_n(k)}(k)=d.

ED26-P15-CH-hypothesis-tests-and-confidence-C017 (partial): The full proof promised by proved=annex:p15.binomial.beta.quantiles is not supplied. The upper formula u_n(k)=Q_{k+1,n-k}(1-d) rests on F_{n,p}(k)=1-I_p(k+1,n-k) for k<n, which annex 690-693 asserts only with 'Likewise'. Neither route to it is written: F_{n,p}(k)=1-T_{n,p}(k+1) combined with the proved identity at k+1, or a comparison of derivatives and initial values.

ED26-P15-CH-neyman-confidence-constructions-C001 (partial): The identified source variant is not preserved, and the corrected procedure is attributed to the source without qualification. The entry gives source Example I's sum system as A_2^U(t)={qt<=S<=(2-q)t} (half-width (1-q)t) with inversion [S/(2-q),S/q]. The held source (Neyman 1937 p. 357, eqs. (46)-(48)) instead computes (47) P=1-(Delta/theta)^2 with Delta=theta(1-alpha)^{1/2}, which gives theta(1-(1-alpha)^{1/2})<=x1+x2<=theta(1+(1-alpha)^{1/2}) and limits (x1+x2)/(1+-(1-alpha)^{1/2}) (p. 358, eqs. (50)-(51)). The two versions agree only at alpha=3/4. The entry marks its boundary choices for A_1^U and A_3^U, but it neither records the source's printed band nor marks its own band as a correction. The source variant is therefore not preserved, and attributing this band to Example I is unsupported.

ED26-P15-CH-neyman-confidence-constructions-C003 (partial): The identified source variant is not preserved. The theorem is titled as the source's length comparisons, yet it states D_2=2(1-q)S/(q(2-q)) and general-alpha bounds (2-q)/4<=D_3/D_2<(2-q)/2. The held source gives the length of its sum interval as delta_2=2(x1+x2)(1-alpha)^{1/2}/alpha (Neyman 1937 p. 358, eq. (52)) and makes its comparison only at alpha=3/4 (pp. 360-362, eqs. (64)-(69)), where the two formulas agree. The source's (52) is not recorded, and the general-alpha comparison is not distinguished from the source's alpha=3/4 comparison.

ED26-P15-CH-neyman-confidence-constructions-C017 (partial): The full proof promised by proved=annex:p15.neyman.normal.one.sided is not supplied. Two claims rest on annex 628-635, 'the same argument makes A^+_t=[t-sigma z_alpha,inf) the unique minimizing acceptance region': the best-one-sided criterion for the upper interval (-inf, X+sigma z_alpha], and the nonexistence argument's use of a unique minimizer on the side s<t. For this direction, three steps are not written: the Neyman-Pearson application for the decreasing likelihood ratio, the identification of the minimizing acceptance set, and its a.e. uniqueness.
